version.changelog: Initial release: cron management, manual run, delivery troubleshooting, dedupe

llm.summary: The skill's commands, files, and instructions are coherent with managing a single OpenClaw cron job for OzBargain, but it references user-specific filesystem paths and logs without declaring them and the package has no external source metadata — verify those before use.

dimensions.detail: Name and description match the included instructions and script: everything is about running/editing an OpenClaw cron job (jobId a3615f3c-8c0d-...). The provided manual_run.sh simply wraps the same openclaw commands documented in SKILL.md — consistent with the stated purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md explicitly instructs the agent to read and update a dedupe state file (/home/kevin/.openclaw/workspace/data/ozbargain-sent-links.json) and to grep OpenClaw log files in /tmp. Those file accesses are directly relevant to deduplication and troubleshooting, but the skill did not declare required config paths. The instructions also invoke openclaw CLI commands and Telegram delivery checks, which are expected for this task.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Instruction-only skill with no install spec and a tiny helper script. No downloads or archive extraction. Low install risk.

dimensions.detail: The skill requires access to the user's OpenClaw workspace and logs but declares no environment variables or required config paths. No credentials are requested by the skill itself — it relies on the existing OpenClaw/Telegram configuration to perform delivery. Confirm that OpenClaw/Telegram credentials are already and intentionally configured elsewhere.

llm.guidance: This skill appears to do what it says: run and manage the specific OpenClaw cron job and handle deduplication. Before installing or enabling it: 1) verify the jobId and that you (or Kevin) expect the skill to read/write /home/kevin/.openclaw/workspace/data/ozbargain-sent-links.json and to inspect /tmp/openclaw logs; 2) confirm the OpenClaw/Telegram bot configuration is trusted and that the bot has appropriate permissions in the target group; 3) because the package source/homepage is unknown, inspect the SKILL.md and scripts (you already have) and confirm there are no additional hidden files or network endpoints; 4) if this will run on an account that is not 'kevin', update paths and verify file ownership/permissions. If any of those items are unclear or you don't want the skill to read/write the dedupe file or logs, do not enable it until clarified.
